title: A Simple Method to Efficiently Record Caenorhabditis elegans Locomotory Behaviours
author: Vishnu Raj
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.uu9ewz6

steps.title: Assemble microscope and stage hardware
steps.instruction: Set up the imaging platform by mounting the Dino‑Lite digital microscope (Model AM4113T‑GFBW) on a tabletop stand (RK‑10) attached to a burette stand with clamps, then place the X‑Y stage on a custom‑made metal frame and position the petri dish with worms on a transparent acrylic sheet on the stage (or directly on the stage if it has a universal holder).

substeps.instruction: Mount the Dino‑Lite digital microscope (Model AM4113T‑GFBW) on the tabletop stand (RK‑10) using the burette‑stand clamps.
Place the X‑Y stage onto the custom‑made metal frame.
Position the petri dish containing worms on a transparent acrylic sheet placed on the X‑Y stage (or directly on the stage if it includes a universal holder).

steps.title: Configure illumination with acrylic sheets
steps.instruction: Install a 7 W white LED light source and arrange white and red acrylic sheets to achieve uniform, high‑contrast illumination, adjusting distances as specified and keeping the sheets parallel.

substeps.instruction: Place the 7 W white LED light source.
Position the white acrylic sheet between the LED and the sample; adjust the gap to 4–7 cm based on the required light intensity.
Place the red acrylic sheet behind the white sheet and set the distance between the white and red sheets to 7–15 cm.
Ensure that the white and red acrylic sheets are parallel to each other.

steps.title: Connect microscope and record video
steps.instruction: Link the USB microscope to a computer via USB cable, launch the Dino‑Lite software module (Dinocapure2.0), and capture video of the worms.

substeps.instruction: Connect the USB microscope to the computer using the USB cable.
Start video recording of the worms.
